skill.name: find-bugs
skill.description: Find bugs, security vulnerabilities, and code quality issues in local branch changes. Use when asked to review changes, find bugs, security review, or audit code on the current branch.
skill.summary: Review local branch changes for bugs, security vulnerabilities, and code quality issues.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a Markdown code span that shows a fixed git diff command. This is not Ruby backtick execution or executable skill code, and no prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: 1. Get the FULL diff: `git diff master...HEAD`

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 12 contains a Markdown inline command, not Ruby or shell backtick execution in executable code. The command is a fixed, read-only git diff used for local review context.

content.value_statement: Branch reviews often miss security bugs, edge cases, and missing verification. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a structured audit of local changes.
actual_capabilities: Reviews the full local branch diff against the master branch.
Maps user inputs, database queries, auth checks, state changes, external calls, and crypto use.
Applies a security checklist covering injection, XSS, CSRF, authorization, sessions, disclosure, DoS, and logic bugs.
Verifies suspected issues against surrounding code and existing tests before reporting.
Ranks findings by severity and includes problem, evidence, fix, and references.
Reports when no significant evidence-backed issues are found.
limitations: Requires access to the local branch and changed files.
Does not modify files or apply fixes.
May miss issues outside the branch diff unless broader review is requested.
Does not replace runtime testing, fuzzing, or manual exploit validation.

use_cases.title: Pre-Merge Security Review
use_cases.description: Audit a branch before merge and receive evidence-backed findings ranked by severity.

use_cases.title: Reviewer Checklist Support
use_cases.description: Use a consistent checklist when reviewing authentication, authorization, input handling, and state changes.

use_cases.title: Release Risk Sweep
use_cases.description: Check high-risk changes for bugs, missing tests, and security regressions before release.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Branch Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of current branch changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use find-bugs to review my current branch. Prioritize security vulnerabilities, bugs, and clear quality issues.

prompt_templates.title: Focused Security Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use find-bugs on this branch with special focus on authentication, authorization, input validation, and information disclosure.

prompt_templates.title: Pre-Merge Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Validate a pull request before merge.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use find-bugs before merge. Read every changed file, verify suspected issues against tests, and report only evidence-backed findings.

prompt_templates.title: High-Risk Change Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Audit payment, account, or permission changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use find-bugs for this payment and account-management change. Map inputs, state transitions, database writes, and external calls before findings.

output_examples.input: Review this login branch for security bugs.
output_examples.output: A severity-ranked list of login risks, evidence for each issue, affected file locations, and concrete fix guidance.

output_examples.input: Check this branch before I merge it.
output_examples.output: A concise review covering changed files, verified findings, clean areas, unverified areas, and suggested next steps.

output_examples.input: Focus on authorization issues in this account update.
output_examples.output: A targeted authorization review that traces access checks, user-controlled identifiers, state changes, and missing test coverage.

best_practices: Run the skill after tests pass and before opening or merging a pull request.
Ask for extra focus on sensitive domains such as payments, identity, permissions, or data export.
Provide context about intended behavior when business rules are not obvious from code.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a replacement for unit tests, integration tests, or security testing.
Do not ask it to report style-only issues when the goal is risk review.
Do not accept findings without checking the cited code and intended behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill change my files?
faq.answer: No. It instructs the assistant to review changes and report findings only.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What types of bugs does it prioritize?
faq.answer: It prioritizes security vulnerabilities first, then functional bugs and meaningful code quality issues.

faq.question: Does it require a Git branch?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow expects local branch changes that can be compared against the master branch.

faq.question: Will it find every vulnerability?
faq.answer: No. It improves review coverage, but it cannot guarantee complete vulnerability detection.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before merging risky changes, during pull request review, or before a release.
